name: Planet Earth and Beyond
what_is_it: Planet Earth and Beyond studies the systems that make Earth work — the water cycle, the atmosphere, weather, and Earth's place in the solar system.
why_it_matters: These systems explain the weather we experience daily, why we have seasons, where our drinking water comes from, and how climate change affects the planet — knowledge essential for environmental awareness and everyday decision-making.
key_vocabulary: Water cycle — the continuous movement of water between the atmosphere, land, and oceans
Evaporation — liquid water turning into water vapour (gas), usually due to heat from the sun
Condensation — water vapour cooling and turning back into liquid water droplets (forming clouds)
Precipitation — water falling from clouds as rain, snow, sleet or hail
Atmosphere — the layer of gases surrounding the Earth, held in place by gravity
Solar system — the Sun and all the objects (planets, moons, asteroids, comets) that orbit it
Orbit — the curved path an object takes around another object due to gravity
Rotation — Earth spinning on its own axis, causing day and night (takes 24 hours)
Revolution — Earth travelling all the way around the Sun (takes about 365.25 days, giving us a year)
core_concept: The water cycle is powered by the Sun's energy: heat causes evaporation, water vapour rises and cools to condense into clouds, and gravity eventually pulls the water back down as precipitation — a continuous, never-ending loop.
key_facts: The Sun's heat is the driving force behind evaporation and therefore the entire water cycle.
Earth's rotation on its axis (24 hours) causes day and night.
Earth's revolution around the Sun (about 365.25 days) causes the yearly cycle of seasons, combined with the tilt of Earth's axis.
The atmosphere is made mostly of nitrogen (about 78%) and oxygen (about 21%), with small amounts of other gases including carbon dioxide.
Water on Earth is constantly recycled — the same water molecules have existed on Earth for billions of years, just changing form and location.
common_misconceptions: Thinking rain is 'new' water — it's part of the same water that has been cycling on Earth for billions of years.
Believing seasons are caused by Earth being closer to or further from the Sun — they're actually caused by the tilt of Earth's axis.
Confusing rotation (day/night, 24 hours) with revolution (a full year around the Sun).
Assuming clouds are made of water vapour — clouds are actually tiny liquid water droplets (or ice crystals) formed by condensation, not gas.
